subject: Preparing a room for installation
hook: Fitting day runs smoother when the room is ready. Here's the prep list we'd hand any customer.
ig:
Fitting day runs smoother when the room is ready. Here's the prep list we'd hand any customer.

Most delays on an installation have nothing to do with the furniture. They come from a wall that's still damp, a socket in the wrong place or a staircase nobody measured.

So before your fitted furniture arrives:

1. Clear the wall where units are going, including old shelves, brackets and TV mounts.
2. Get plastering, electrics and plumbing finished and dry first.
3. Walk the route from the front door to the room and note any tight turns.
4. Decide whether flooring goes down before or after the furniture.
5. Confirm where every socket, switch and pipe will sit.
6. Keep a clear working area in front of the wall on the day.

We go through all of this at the measuring visit, so nothing surprises anyone on fit day. The list just helps you get ahead of it.

If you're planning a kitchen, wardrobe or media wall this spring, save this post and book a free design consultation through the link in bio.

If you spent the Easter break clearing out a room ready for new furniture, this one's for you.

The smoothest installations we do are the ones where the room is properly ready: walls clear, plastering dry, electrics finished, and a clear route from the van to the room. It sounds obvious, but a damp wall or a socket that needs moving can hold up a fitter far more than the furniture itself ever will.

We've put the full prep checklist in the carousel. Have a flick through, and if you're planning fitted furniture anywhere around Stoke-on-Trent, we'll go through it all with you at a free, no-obligation consultation.

on_asset: S1: Before the fitters arrive | Six jobs that make fit day easier | S2: Clear the whole wall — Pictures, shelves, curtain poles and wall-mounted TVs come down wherever furniture is going. Old fixings left in the wall can clash with new panels. | S3: Finish the messy trades first — Plastering, rewiring and plumbing changes should be finished and dry before furniture goes in. Dust and damp are no friend to new panels. | S4: Check the route in — Tall panels and long worktops need a clear path from the van: front door, hallway, stairs, landing. Mention tight turns at the survey. | S5: Agree the flooring order — Some rooms suit flooring laid first, others fitted up to the furniture. Settle it with your maker before the day, not on it. | S6: Fix socket and pipe positions — Anything that ends up behind or inside furniture needs agreeing at design stage, so cut-outs and access panels are planned in. | S7: A ready room means a cleaner fit — Save this list for your project.
